Class EfsFile<E extends IEfsEvent>

java.lang.Object
org.efs.io.EfsFile<E>
Type Parameters:
E - efs event type.
All Implemented Interfaces:
IEfsAgent
@ThreadSafe public final class EfsFile<E extends IEfsEvent> extends Object implements IEfsAgent
In-memory event file for a single event type + topic.

An EfsFile stores events (instances of IEfsEvent) and assigns each posted event:

  • a publish timestamp (an Instant obtained from the system clock), and
  • a monotonic, continuous row index (a long) that is unique within the file.

The file keeps events in a CQEngine indexed collection so callers can query historical events (by timestamp or row index) and optionally subscribe to future events that match an interval and a CQEngine Query.

Threading and postRow

EfsFile is thread-safe. All public operations that mutate or query file state are handed off to the file's associated dispatcher (see EfsDispatcher) so that event delivery and request completion happen on the dispatcher's thread. This provides a virtual single-threaded processing model for agents interacting with a particular EfsFile.

Lifecycle

  • Create with EfsFile.Builder. A Builder instance is acquired from builder(EfsTopicKey). Builder requires only that a dispatcher name is set (since EfsFile is itself an agent). This dispatcher name must correspond to a dispatcher created/started by your application.
  • Obtain a connection using connect(AccessMode, org.efs.dispatcher.IEfsAgent). The agent must be registered with the dispatcher before calling connect.
  • Use the returned EfsFileConnection to add events or to EfsFileConnection.retrieve(org.efs.io.EfsInterval, com.googlecode.cqengine.query.Query, java.util.function.Consumer, java.util.function.Consumer) historical and/or future events.
  • Close EfsFileConnections when finished; doClose the file with close() to remove it from the global registry.

Ordering and Consistency Guarantees

  • Row Index: Strictly increasing, unique, and assigned in the order events are posted. Can be used as a linearization point.
  • Publish Timestamp: Non-decreasing (monotonic) but not guaranteed unique. Events posted in quick succession may share the same timestamp. When two rows have the same timestamp, they are ordered by row index in ascending order.
  • Query Results: Always returned in ascending row index order, ensuring a consistent linearization across historical and future retrievals.
  • Retrieval Continuity: A retrieval that spans both historical and future events will never skip or duplicate a row, even if the historical query and future subscriptions are processed asynchronously.

Querying

EfsFile exposes a small set of CQEngine attributes and provides event-field attributes:

  • ROW_INDEX_ATTRIBUTE — row index attribute name.
  • PUBLISH_TIMESTAMP_ATTRIBUTE — publish timestamp attribute name.
  • Use attribute(String) to obtain a CQEngine Attribute<EfsRow<E>,?> for event fields extracted from the event class layout; that attribute can be used in CQEngine queries.

A CQEngine Query<EfsRow<E>> is required when calling EfsFileConnection.retrieve(...). For simple retrieval of all rows in an interval, combine CQEngine interval queries (by index or timestamp) with a user query (or a query that matches all rows).

Errors and exceptional states

  • Passing a null topic key, dispatcher, access mode, or agent will throw NullPointerException.
  • Creating a file for a key that already exists will throw IllegalStateException.
  • Connecting with an agent that is not registered with a dispatcher will throw IllegalStateException.
  • Attempting to add events on a connection opened without write permission or retrieving on a read-only connection will throw IllegalStateException.

Example (simplified)

// Create or obtain a dispatcher named "mainDispatcher" before calling createEventFile.
// (See org.efs.dispatcher.EfsDispatcher.Builder for creating dispatchers.)

// Define the topic key for an event type
EfsTopicKey<MyEvent> key = EfsTopicKey.getKey(MyEvent.class, "myTopic");

// Create the file (registers it with the given dispatcher)
EfsFile<MyEvent> file = EfsFile.createEventFile(key, "mainDispatcher");

// Assuming 'agent' is an IEfsAgent instance that has been registered with the same dispatcher:
EfsFileConnection<MyEvent> conn = file.connect(AccessMode.READ_WRITE, agent);

// Append an event (returns the publish Instant)
Instant publishedAt = conn.add(new MyEvent(...));

// Build an interval (example: from 1 hour ago until now, inclusive)
EfsInterval interval = EfsInterval.builder()
    .beginning(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder().timeOffset(Duration.ofHours(-1), EfsIntervalEndpoint.Clusivity.INCLUSIVE).build())
    .ending(EfsDurationEndpoint.builder().now(EfsIntervalEndpoint.Clusivity.INCLUSIVE).build())
    .build();

// Create a CQEngine query that matches the events you want (user-provided).
// For example, you can use attributes returned by file.attribute("fieldName").
Query<EfsRow<MyEvent>> query = /* create your CQEngine query for EfsRow<MyEvent> * /;

// Retrieve matching events and subscribe to completion callback
EfsFileConnection.Retrieval<MyEvent> r =
    conn.retrieve(interval,
                  query,
                  row -> {
                      // event callback: row.getEvent() or row.getRowIndex()/getPublishTimestamp()
                  },
                  completionEvent -> {
                      // completion callback: check completionEvent.completionType()
                  });

// When finished, cancel retrieval (AutoCloseable)
r.doClose();
conn.doClose();
file.doClose();

Note: the example is illustrative and omits dispatcher and agent setup details. See the dispatcher package documentation for how to create and register dispatchers and agents.

    • setSystemClock

      public Clock setSystemClock(Clock clock)
      Sets system clock used to obtain Instant values, returning replaced system clock. This method is mainly used by unit tests to put a fixed clock in place. This allows for tests to always use the same time.

      Note: setting this system clock affects all active EfsFile instances. This method is primarily provided for unit tests which need to control wall clock time for consistent test results. If used, that means that tests updating the system clock may not execute in parallel as these tests will impact the other and prevent consistent test results. Therefore when using this method in testing, parallel execution is discouraged.

      This method may also be used to replace the default Clock.systemUTC() with a proprietary clock. This should be during application start up.

      Parameters:
      clock - replaces current system clock.
      Returns:
      replaced system clock.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if clock is null.

    • connect

      public EfsFileConnection<E> connect(EfsFile.AccessMode accessMode, IEfsAgent agent)
      Returns an EfsFileConnection instance for given connection mode and agent.
      Parameters:
      accessMode - event file connect mode.
      agent - agent accessing event file.
      Returns:
      efs event file connect instance.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if either accessMode or agent is null.
      IllegalStateException - if:
      • agent is not registered with a dispatcher,
      • this file is closed,
      • agent is not allowed to connect with this file using accessMode, or
      • this file's connection limit is at maximum and no new connections are allowed until an existing connection closes.

    • close

      public void close()
      Closes this efs event file asynchronously on dispatcher thread. All stored events are lost. Does nothing if already closed.
